items.title: Anwar vows to strengthen MITRA and expand Indian community support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Indian community will not be sidelined in the national development agenda, with the Madani government continuing to expand efforts to improve the community’s standard of living, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the efforts included widening access to financing for entrepreneurs, strengthening the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), enhancing entrepreneurship and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and creating more opportunities for youth development through mentor-mentee programmes. “Various efforts have been undertaken in education, entrepreneurship, microfinancing, welfare and cash assistance to ease the burden on families and improve their standard of living,” he said in a Facebook post last night.

items.title: Three teenage girls involved in scuffle over photo
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Police are investigating a fight involving three teenage girls at Dataran Melang here that went viral on social media. Kuala Pilah police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said police received a report over the incident last Wednesday. Those with information can contact the Kuala Pilah district police headquarters at 06-48429999, investigating officer Sergeant Shamsuldalila Mohamad at 011-10129038, or any nearby police station.

items.title: Sarawak haze pushes Serian API reading to 495, just short of ‘emergency’ level
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 4 — Haze in Serian worsened sharply overnight, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) there climbing to 495 this morning, just five points below the level that would trigger an “emergency” declaration. The Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) recorded the reading at the Serian monitoring station at 7am today, making it the only locality in the country with a hazardous reading. Sarawak Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas previously said a locality would be declared an emergency if its API reading reached 500.

items.title: Nepal tragedy: Support group seeks Tamil counsellors for victims’ families
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Solidariti Malaysia: Keluarga Dalam Harapan (MASFIH), a support group for families of victims in the Nepal flash flood tragedy, has appealed for certified Tamil-speaking counsellors to provide psychological support to affected relatives. He said using third-party translators during therapy sessions was unsuitable as it could affect the emotional connection families needed during this difficult time. “The families themselves must come forward.

items.title: #NSTviral: Tunku Azizah steals the show in surprise TikTok livestream appearance [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A TikTok livestream at a boutique in Bangsar took an unexpected turn when Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, dropped by and joined the staff on camera. Tunku even joined our TikTok livestream with our staff," it said. "Aww, Tunku Azizah is so adorable.

items.title: 'Subpoenaed to attend TH RCI, but told to go home' - Madinah
items.summary: Madinah said claims made by TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussain , who is also an RCI member, regarding her attendance at the proceedings were inaccurate. She said she had never asked to enter the RCI hearing room with then National Audit Department Financial Audit Division deputy director Dr Mona Othman. "I never asked to enter the hearing room with Mona.

items.title: Ramanan: PM discussed Budget 2027 with Indian community leaders and NGOs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Education, economic opportunities, welfare and socioeconomic development were among the key issues discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Indian community leaders yesterday. Human Resources Minister R. Ramanan said the second session of the meeting brought together leaders from nine chambers of commerce and 14 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to discuss community perspectives, including inputs for Budget 2027. He said the meeting represented the government’s ongoing effort to directly listen to and understand the views, aspirations and challenges faced by the Indian community.

items.title: Ringgit opens firmer against greenback after Bank Negara holds OPR
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar on Friday, buoyed by improved sentiment after Bank Negara Malaysia kept its overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75 per cent. Meanwhile, Mohd Afzanizam said the ringgit also benefited from a softer US dollar following US Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller's remarks overnight, which reduced expectations of a rate hike at the Fed's September meeting. "This US dollar weakness is broadly supportive of emerging market currencies, including the ringgit," he said.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls for Penang fee, quit rent and water tariff hikes to be deferred
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has urged the Penang government to emulate Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim by deferring increases in fees, quit rent and water tariffs to ease the financial burden on businesses and households. Lim said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and state executive councillor Zairil Khir Johari should adopt the same reformist approach and political will to fulfil the election manifesto and ease the cost of living for Penang residents. He said the increase would generate an additional RM20 million a year for Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP), but would have a negative impact on 1.8 million Penang residents.

items.title: Teen TVET student found drowned after disappearing while crab hunting in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 4 — A teenager, believed to have gone missing while looking for crabs in the coastal reclamation area near Pantai Klebang here, was found drowned late yesterday. Melaka Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Fire and Rescue Operations Division, Senior Fire Superintendent II Mohd Shahrom Laji, said Muhammad Arif Daniel Nizamuddin, 16, a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institution student, was found near the waters of Pulau Upeh at about 7:20 pm yesterday. “The victim was found by fishermen near Pulau Upeh, about two nautical miles from the mainland, before the Search and Rescue team went to the location to retrieve the victim’s body.

items.title: PAS targets prime minister’s post, says no more ‘giving way’ to other parties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — PAS Youth delegates have urged the party to lead cooperation with other political parties while insisting that it has enough qualified candidates to lead the federal government. PAS Kedah Youth chief Ilyas Ahmad said efforts to unite Muslims at the federal level should be led by PAS, which he said should no longer make way for other parties to put forward the prime ministerial candidate, according to a Malaysiakini report. This time, we want to ensure PAS becomes the main leader at the federal level,” he said.

items.title: 'Do not leave your fate in the hands of the elite' - Sanusi
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The elite should no longer determine the country's direction, with ordinary Malaysians now needing to rise and have a greater say in shaping the nation's future, said Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor. He said the elite made up only about 10 per cent of Malaysia's population but controlled a large share of the country's wealth. Sanusi said the elite not only did not understand the everyday language used by ordinary people, let alone the realities and hardships they faced.

items.title: RNG Tech Thai unit lands exclusive Lotus's massage chair deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: RNG Tech Bhd's Thai unit has secured a three-and-a-half-year partnership with CP Axtra Public Company Ltd to exclusively provide and operate massage chairs at selected Lotus's stores across Thailand. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said Rest n Go (Thailand) Company Ltd entered into a memorandum of agreement with CP Axtra on Sept 2, covering Lotus's hypermarkets, supermarkets and community malls. Rest n Go Thailand won a Lotus's tender in 2025 and currently operates 806 massage chairs across 132 Lotus's locations in the country.

items.title: How Zetrix bet on its future and lost two-thirds of its value
items.summary: On Aug 28, just two days after Zetrix made its last share buyback of 933,300 shares at 66.5 sen apiece, Wong disposed of 99.8 million shares at 29.9 sen apiece, at a time when the counter had traded around 60 sen earlier in the day. Some 4.29 million shares were disposed of on Aug 27 at 60.6 sen apiece, followed by another 52.3 million shares on Aug 28 at 48 sen apiece. Zetrix's share price had not fallen below 60 sen before Aug 27.

items.title: Gambling ban already Pas policy, no need for manifesto - Sanusi
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas does not need to include its opposition to gambling in its election manifesto as the stance is already enshrined in the party's Islamic principles, said Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor. Sanusi, who is also Pas election director said society should rely on their effort, prayer and tawakal (trust in God) to achieve success in life, rather than turning to gambling. "Islam prohibits gambling!

items.title: FMM backs 3pct GST to cut manufacturers' tax burden
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing (FMM) is pushing for a 3.0 per cent Goods and Services Tax (GST) as a way to ease tax-related cost pressures on manufacturers, but a tax expert said the proposed rate should be considered alongside its potential impact on government revenue. FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said the proposed introductory rate, which is half the previous 6.0 per cent GST rate, would be a more acceptable starting point for businesses and consumers while giving manufacturers greater capacity to reinvest and improve productivity. FMM's push comes amid concerns over the cost implications of the current Sales and Services Tax (SST) regime.

items.title: Firm demand backs Bank Negara's 2.75pct OPR hold: experts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent despite stronger economic growth reflects confidence that domestic demand remains firm without creating excessive inflationary or financial pressures, an economist said. Universiti Teknologi Malaysia associate professor of property economics Dr Muhammad Najib Razali said the current policy stance gives the economy room to absorb external shocks while keeping borrowing costs supportive of household spending, business investment and infrastructure development. Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7 per cent in the first half of 2026, prompting Bank Negara to expect full-year growth of around five per cent.

items.title: Serian haze worsens, API hits 495
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions in Serian, Sarawak, have worsened, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) rising to 495 as of 7am today. Three locations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, with Kuching recording 289, followed by Samarahan (265) and Sri Aman (250). Six other areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Sarikei (181), Sibu (174), Mukah (169), Bintulu (159), Samalaju (153) and ILP Miri (149).

items.title: 'Zero updates': Families demand answers over missing Malaysians in Nepal [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Desperation has gripped the families of Malaysians still missing after the devastating floods in Nepal. M. Subramaniam, 38, said families had repeatedly given authorities the names, photographs, personal details and last known locations of those missing, including his 74-year-old father-in-law, retired civil servant Krishnan Vadivelu. Subramaniam said some family members had travelled to Nepal to get information of their loved ones.

items.title: OpenAI begins rollout of new powerful AI model GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: ChatGPT maker OpenAI said Thursday it would begin rolling out its newest and most powerful artificial intelligence (AI) model to select customers, saying it had built in safeguards to mitigate security risks. Just over a year has passed since OpenAI launched the previous version of its flagship model, GPT-5. OpenAI paused some model development for two weeks this summer after two models it was testing were involved in a security breach at AI platform Hugging Face.

items.title: The rot has to stop: Time to end the plunder of the gravy train
items.summary: We've seen everyone, from administrators, government agency directors, public-listed company chief executives and titled businessmen to political secretaries and even top army officials being escorted in and out of courtrooms for various offences. Who would have thought it possible, especially in a country where cynicism has become something of a national pastime? Yet his legal battles are far from over, with almost daily court appearances to answer another long list of accusations.

items.title: Malaysia’s chip ambitions: From assembly hub to semiconductor powerhouse
items.summary: The country is particularly strong in the back end of the semiconductor supply chain — assembly, packaging and testing — but is seeking a bigger role in higher-value activities such as chip design, advanced packaging, semiconductor equipment and research and development. First, what exactly is a semiconductor? Silicon is the most widely used semiconductor material.

items.title: Iran war is not a war, US VP Vance says
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he would not categorise the Iran war as a war, despite continuing clashes with Teheran six months after the start of the conflict. "I wouldn't call it a war. WEDDING STRIKE PROBE "Their control over the Strait of Hormuz is effectively gone," Vance said of Iran.

items.title: 20 students find journalism spark during Media Prima visit
items.summary: ABOUT 20 Kolej Profesional Mara Seri Iskandar students visited Media Prima Bhd yesterday, where they gained first-hand exposure to newsroom and broadcasting operations. The Diploma in English Communication students visited Balai Berita under Eduscape, an initiative by Media Prima aimed at exposing students to television, radio, print and digital media operations. The students took turns anchoring news at the studio.

items.title: 40 wild elephants roaming forests near Pos Gob
items.summary: ABOUT 40 wild elephants are believed to be roaming the forests around Pos Gob, where their natural migration routes overlap with nearby settlements. Kelantan Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) director Wan Mohd Adib Wan Yusoh said the elephants were part of the ID Nenggiri herd. Wan Mohd Adib said Perhilitan would deploy officers to monitor the area.

items.title: Penang bags RM17.3b in approved manufacturing investments
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang led Malaysia in approved manufacturing investments in the first half of this year, securing RM17.3 billion, according to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida). The figure represented a 38 per cent year-on-year increase from the corresponding period last year, with the state accounting for 34 per cent of Malaysia's total approved manufacturing investments during the six-month period. Of the total, RM12.8 billion came from foreign direct investment (FDI), accounting for 74 per cent of Penang's approved manufacturing investments and 39 per cent of the country's total manufacturing FDI.

items.title: '800 ill in latest Indonesian food poisoning outbreaks'
items.summary: NEARLY 800 Indonesians have fallen ill in separate incidents of food poisoning linked to the government's free meals programme, said a member of a parliamentary commission overseeing health, including more than 500 students in East Java province this week. President Prabowo Subianto launched his multibillion-dollar programme last year to eradicate under-nutrition by giving free meals to tens of millions of children, but the scheme has been dogged by controversies, including mass food poisoning, allegations of corruption, leadership changes and a burdensome price tag. Improper food storage and late delivery of cooked meals are often to blame for the food poisoning, authorities have said.

items.title: Ahead of elections, Israel tests West's patience on West Bank violence
items.summary: While many observers expect caution from Western states in their responses before the elections, Britain's foreign secretary on Tuesday vowed a major policy reset towards Israel's West Bank construction and promised a "comprehensive set of measures" within weeks. A Tel Aviv-based European diplomat told AFP that the idea of taking measures against Israel once seemed "completely unthinkable." Israel has fought against foreign governments making any distinction between goods from Israel and West Bank settlements.

items.title: Thailand scraps 60-day visa-free entry, reinstates 30-day scheme
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand will implement a major overhaul of its tourist visa exemption and visa‑on‑arrival rules from Sept 15, officially ending the 60‑day exemption scheme introduced two years ago, the Foreign Ministry announced. Under the revised framework approved by Cabinet, Thailand will reintroduce a 30‑day visa‑free entry scheme, introduce a new 15‑day exemption category for select countries, and restructure the visa‑on‑arrival list. A new 15‑day exemption covers travellers from two countries, while visa‑on‑arrival is narrowed to three nations.

items.title: Indonesia rescues 11 orangutans as wildfire approaches rehabilitation centre
items.summary: JAKARTA: Eleven orangutans were evacuated from a rehabilitation centre in East Kalimantan as forest fires closed in, Indonesian authorities confirmed, activating emergency measures to protect the endangered primates. Ari Wibawanto, head of the East Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency (BKSDA), said emergency status was declared at the Jejak Pulang Forest School in Samboja, Kutai Kartanegara regency, on Sept 1 after smoke and flames began approaching. The orangutans undergoing rehabilitation were moved to a temporary care facility.

items.title: Indonesian police bust online gambling network generating US$56.6mil annually
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian police have dismantled a multimillion‑rupiah online gambling network operating three overseas‑based websites, arresting five suspects in a crackdown that exposed transactions worth more than 1 trillion rupiah (about US$56.6 million) annually. Police said the network processed over 1.03 trillion rupiah in transactions between January and August, averaging 8.6 billion rupiah daily. Authorities have frozen about 51 billion rupiah held by five payment service providers.

items.title: Three killed after jumping from burning factory in Indonesia
items.summary: JAKARTA: Three construction workers plunged to their deaths after leaping from the sixth floor of a burning soap factory in Indonesia's North Sumatra province on Thursday, local police confirmed. The fire broke out around 10am at the Evyap Sabun Indonesia factory in the Sei Mangkei Special Economic Zone, Simalungun regency, police spokesperson Verry Purba said. Firefighters were still battling the flames more than three hours later, while the cause remained under investigation.– BERNAMA © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Umno must choose government or quit if it favours PN, says PKR Youth leader
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A PKR Youth leader has challenged Umno to either commit to the unity government or relinquish its positions in the government if the party is in favour of Perikatan Nasional. PKR Youth deputy chief Nabil Halimi said Umno should not be seen as having one foot in the unity government while simultaneously cooperating with the opposition. "If they want to join PN, then make that decision and relinquish their positions in the government.

items.title: Mechanic injured after gunmen open fire at workshop
items.summary: The victim is believed to have lodged a police report with the Kulim police station in Kedah before being sent to hospital for treatment. Police are investigating the motive and said the victim has a previous criminal record. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng, when contacted, confirmed the incident.

items.title: 12-year-old boy killed in Gurun crash involving motorcycle, two lorries
items.summary: GURUN: A 12-year-old boy was killed in an accident involving a motorcycle and two lorries at Masjid Batu 3, Jalan Jeniang, here today. The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre (PGO) said it received a distress call via the NG999 line at 1.36pm. Based on information from the caller, a victim was trapped under a lorry, prompting the PGO to dispatch an LFRT fire engine and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle from the Guar Chempedak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene.

items.title: El Nino could be strongest in four decades, UN warns
items.summary: El Nino will peak towards the end of this year – though its knock-on impacts for the climate will continue well into 2027, said the WMO. El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall. "El Nino is being supersized before our eyes," said UN chief Antonio Guterres.

items.title: TVET student missing while catching crabs found drowned
items.summary: MELAKA: A teenage boy who went missing at Pantai Klebang while catching crabs with friends yesterday was found floating near Pulau Upeh today. Melaka Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Mohd Shahrom Laji said the victim was identified by his family at 8.30pm. He said the search and rescue (SAR) operation began yesterday, with the department's Water Rescue Team conducting a solo search around the area where the teenager was last seen.

items.title: Lebanon receives first detainee of five to be freed by Israel
items.summary: BEIRUT: Lebanon said it received a man on Thursday freed as Israel announced it would release five people seized from the country's south, where it has fought several wars against Iran-backed Hizbollah in recent years. The announcement came after Lebanon said its army received a man returned by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the first since Beirut called in August talks for the release of an initial group seized since the start of a 2024 Israel-Hizbollah war. "It was decided to release five Lebanese civilians who were arrested in areas under (Israeli army) control in southern Lebanon," the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement.

items.title: Increase to 22 special draws was a collective responsibility of previous government, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The decision to increase the number of special forecast number draws to 22 times a year during the previous administration was a collective responsibility of the Cabinet, including ministers from PAS at the time, said former Finance Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. Tengku Zafrul, who is now the Senior Political Adviser to the Prime Minister, said special draws are not new as they were introduced back in 1999, and the ceiling limit of 22 draws a year already existed during the Barisan Nasional administration before he was appointed as Finance Minister. “Importantly, under today’s Madani Government, the special draws have been reduced to just eight times a year,” he told Bernama today.

items.title: Serian records hazardous API 391, four other Sarawak areas at very unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, September 3 — Air quality continued to deteriorate this afternoon, with Serian in Sarawak recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 391, putting it in the hazardous category, while four other areas in the state recorded very unhealthy readings. Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said four areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Kuching registering an API reading of 285, Sri Aman 275, Samarahan 274 and Sarikei 206. Eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy air quality, with Sibu registering an API reading of 180, followed by Mukah (172), Bintulu (166), Samalaju (164), Kapit (157), ILP Miri (153), Limbang (151) and Miri (106).

items.title: Contractor: Muhyiddin’s Bersatu donation request wasn’t my imagination, I didn’t report it fearing abetment accusations
items.summary: Azman: Disagree. But Azman disagreed. Azman disagreed.

items.title: Malaysia probes claim subsidised padi fertiliser smuggled into Thailand for bomb-making
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH, September 3 — Malaysia and Thailand will use existing bilateral mechanisms to investigate allegations of bomb-making activities involving fertiliser elements from Malaysia, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the Malaysian and Thai police would conduct their respective investigations, with the matter to be managed through established channels, including government-to-government engagement, the Border Working Group and Police-to-Police (P-to-P) cooperation. Meanwhile, the Border Working Group serves as another platform for Malaysia and Thailand to discuss matters concerning the border, he said.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher, FBM KLCI gains 6.39 points as BNM holds OPR
items.summary: Turnover declined to 3.90 billion units valued at RM3.21 billion from 4.20 billion units valued at RM3.52 billion on Wednesday. Warrants turnover expanded to 995.66 million units worth RM132.91 million versus 942.18 billion units worth RM133.94 million previously. The ACE Market volume trimmed to 515.65 million units valued at RM199.58 million from 592.31 million units valued at RM176.71 million yesterday.

items.title: MetMalaysia conducts cloud seeding over Perlis, Kedah to boost dam water levels
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, September 3 — The government has carried out a cloud seeding operation (OPA) in Perlis and Kedah today as an early, targeted measure to address dry weather, low rainfall and deteriorating air quality risks. A Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) C-130H aircraft from No. 20 Squadron, Subang Air Base, was used for the operation, carrying four tanks of salt solution for cloud seeding.

items.title: ‘You were supposed to come back today’: Wife marks anniversary as firefighter husband remains missing in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A 10th wedding anniversary, an occasion that should have been marked with gifts and quality time together, has instead become a period of anxious waiting for Hani Othman, whose husband, Senior Fire Officer II (PBK II) Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, remains missing following a flood tragedy in Rasuwa, Nepal, on August 26. Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, who remains missing following floods in Nepal, is pictured with his wife, Hani Othman. Hani wrote.

items.title: Rising airfares could undermine Visit Sabah 2027 tourism push, says former state Matta chief
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 3 — The government should consider targeted assistance or subsidies to address rising airfares and fuel costs that could undermine Sabah’s tourism competitiveness ahead of Visit Sabah 2027, said former Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (Matta) Sabah chairman Mohd Azlan Saleh Abd Salam. He said high travel costs could prompt tourists to choose other destinations in the region offering more competitive prices, particularly as Sabah prepares to ramp up its tourism promotion. He said rising petrol and diesel costs were also putting pressure on tourism operators, including tour bus, van and boat operators.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah: Oil and gas here to stay even as Malaysia pushes for green energy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Oil and gas will continue to play a critical role in supporting Malaysia’s economic growth and safeguarding national energy security, even as the country accelerates its shift toward cleaner energy sources, Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. Speaking at the Oil and Gas Asia Convention, Akmal emphasised that natural gas will remain a major component of Malaysia’s primary energy mix through 2050. Malaysia currently has a relatively diversified energy mix, with natural gas accounting for 42 per cent of total primary energy supply in 2024, followed by crude oil and petroleum products at 33 per cent, coal and coke at 22 per cent, and hydropower and renewables at 4 per cent.

items.title: Malaysia must act now as 10pc US tariff not guaranteed ceiling, says industry expert
items.summary: Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of maritime experience, said the issue was particularly important given the ongoing US investigation into structural excess capacity involving Malaysia and several other economies. Recently, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the US was expected to announce its findings from the excess capacity investigation involving Malaysia within three to four weeks. Johari said the current 10 per cent tariff formed part of broader US action involving 60 economies under Section 301 of the Trade Act 1974, with Malaysia among 17 economies subjected to the lower tariff rate.

items.title: Ipoh police probe viral video of two children sitting on roof of moving MPV
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 3 — Police are investigating a viral video showing two children sitting on the roof of a moving multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), Astro Awani eported. Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police had yet to receive any report regarding the incident. However, he said police were tracing the owner of the vehicle.

items.title: Search continues for two more after second teen confirmed drowned in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The body of one of the three teenagers who went missing while bathing at Tanjung Lompat Beach, Kota Tinggi was found at 1.53 pm today. Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime headquarters operations officer Lieutenant Commander Mohamed Shafiee Bakar said Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, 16, was found floating about 800 metres from the location where the first victim, Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, was found yesterday. He said the victim’s body has been taken for a post-mortem at the Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: Law minister: Coroners Bill to be tabled next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Coroners Bill, aimed at clarifying the management of death cases, is expected to be tabled in Parliament next year, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Azalina said drafting the law is expected to establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and detail the roles of coroners and relevant parties in handling death cases. Azalina said, although procedures for death investigations exist under current legislation, the Coroners Act will complement them and offer clearer guidance on implementation.

items.title: Azalina: PM term limit and AG/PP separation Bills ready for Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A Bill to limit the tenure of the prime minister is ready for its second reading in the Dewan Rakyat, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The limit on the prime minister’s term is ready. Azalina said the proposed term limit for the prime minister would involve amendments to the Federal Constitution and would therefore require the support of a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

items.title: Tabung Haji Act amendments in final stages before parliamentary tabling, says TH CEO
items.summary: BANGI, Sept 3 — The process of amending the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) has now reached 90 per cent at the internal level of the Tabung Haji Board (TH) and is expected to be brought to the Cabinet after the technical process and engagement with relevant parties are finalised. TH chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said the amendment was among the remaining main actions following the 25 recommendations submitted by the TH Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). The remaining six actions include amendments to Act 535; limiting the scope of Bank Negara Malaysia's supervision of TH and strengthening the disciplinary process.

items.title: Senior Citizens Bill delayed to early 2027, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 3 — The Senior Citizens Bill, previously targeted for tabling this October, is expected to be brought to Parliament in early 2027. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said that although the draft bill is complete, the process is taking time due to engagement sessions with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and state governments. The new law aims to provide more comprehensive legal protection, particularly in addressing issues of neglect, abuse, and exploitation involving senior citizens.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Tech advances require modern laws to combat crime
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the increasingly complex challenges required the government and enforcement agencies to adopt a comprehensive approach involving multiple stakeholders. “Increasingly complex threats require a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Nation approach, bringing together the strengths of the government, enforcement agencies, academia, industry, technology providers and international partners,” he said. Knowledge and research findings must be translated into policies, strengthen enforcement capabilities and produce solutions to the real security challenges faced by the people,” he said.

items.title: DOE samples factory discharge after dead fish and crabs found in Sungai Sitiawan
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 3 — The Department of Environment (DOE) has collected industrial effluent samples from a manufacturing factory as part of its investigation into alleged river pollution after fish and crabs were found dead in Sungai Sitiawan. The department said the samples were taken at the premises’ final discharge point to allow investigators to compare them with water samples collected from the river. “Industrial effluent samples were taken at the final discharge point of the premises.

items.title: Penang gazettes Hungry Ghost Festival as state heritage, six sites also set for official recognition
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang has gazetted the Teong Guan Phor Thor, or Hungry Ghost Festival, as a state heritage item under the Penang State Heritage Enactment 2011, recognising a traditional celebration observed by more than 200 groups across the state. The state also approved the designation of six heritage sites on April 8, Chow said. The earlier list comprised 15 heritage sites, 28 food heritage items and seven intangible heritage items.

items.title: Court of Appeal sets aside fraud, conspiracy findings in RM52.2m Johor land dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Court of Appeal has set aside findings of fraud and conspiracy against a businessman and property agent in a dispute over a proposed RM52.2 million sale of a 22ha tract of land in Johor. However, a three-member panel upheld the High Court’s findings that no binding sale agreement had been concluded and that businessman J. Siva Kumar had wrongfully lodged a private caveat over the land. Siva and Ammsa had sought specific performance of an alleged sale and purchase agreement with Firwas.

items.title: SAR area expanded to two nautical miles in search for three missing teenagers in Tanjung Lompat
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for three teenagers missing at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar has been expanded to cover up to two nautical miles of coastal waters today. Tanjung Sedili Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) acting director Mohd Najib Sam said the search area was widened following the discovery of one victim about 500 metres from the incident site yesterday. “Today’s SAR operational area has been increased from one to two nautical miles of coastal area in an effort to locate the three missing teenagers.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi says only Zahid can decide whether he should step down as Mara chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Mara chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said only Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi could decide whether he should step down from the position. “I was appointed by the Deputy Prime Minister, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister. Asyraf said Mara’s reputation and role as a Malay and Bumiputera institution must be protected from efforts to undermine it.
